page: Amazon Web Services r6in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, utilizing third-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, maintaining a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The processor includes 54 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI, and memory protection features like Total Memory Encryption.

The system is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, enabling high-throughput inter-node communication and EBS access. The instance includes zero local instance storage, requiring all persistent and scratch volumes to be attached via networked storage solutions. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs integrated into the configuration.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong multi-threaded compute capabilities, scoring in the upper 25% for PassMark CPU, stress-ng multi-core execution, and software compilation tasks. Synthetic database performance also ranks in the top tier, reflected in a PassMark database operations metric of 26,410.42. Single-core performance and memory bandwidth tests fall within the middle 50% of evaluated hardware, with large-block uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 166.24 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 67.38 GB/sec.

From an operational cost perspective, the r6in.16xlarge offers resource density tailored for large in-memory workloads requiring sustained high network throughput without paying for local solid-state drives or graphical acceleration. Its architecture is suited for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching platforms, real-time analytics engines, and network-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) running at 3.5 GHz, the system pairs high multi-threaded compute capacity with 512 GB of DDR4 system memory and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote network-attached volumes for data persistence. Benchmark results place the instance in the top quartile for multi-core compute throughput, Clang compilation, and database operations, while single-core processing and memory bandwidth remain in the middle tier. This configuration represents an efficient resource balance for memory-intensive applications requiring substantial network throughput, including in-memory distributed caches, enterprise relational databases, real-time ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web services.
